C-1.why: C-1 is AL 218, which Aerolark moved from 07:10 to 11:05, 3 hours 55 minutes later on a domestic itinerary (3 hours or more is significant, 14 CFR 260.2); she declined it and did not fly, and the credit was issued by Aerolark unasked (M-1), so the fare is owed back to her card under 260.6(a). Weighted at the fare, 142.00 dollars

A-1.why: A-1 is the 38 dollar extra-legroom seat fee for AL 330, a seat the substituted aircraft does not have (M-8), through no fault of hers; 260.4 refunds an ancillary fee for a service not provided, automatically, and Aerolark has not. Weighted at the fee, 38.00 dollars

C-6.why: C-6 is SK 804, Boston to Toronto, an international itinerary, moved from 08:15 to 14:45 and 09:50 to 16:20, 6 hours 30 minutes later (6 hours or more is significant on an international itinerary); she declined and did not fly and the credit was Skylindle's, unasked (M-2). Weighted at the fare, 188.00 dollars

C-7.why: C-7 is SK 311, whose times did not change, but which now lands at Newark instead of LaGuardia: a different destination airport is a significant change by itself (260.2), though the notice (M-3) calls it a minor update; she declined and did not fly. Weighted at the fare, 98.00 dollars

C-8.why: C-8 is SK 451, which was non-stop and is now one stop in Chicago, with the times 20 minutes and 25 minutes earlier: more connection points than the original itinerary is a significant change (260.2); she declined and did not fly and the credit was unasked. Weighted at the fare, 210.00 dollars

C-12.why: C-12 is AL 509 bought through Tripcairn, moved by Aerolark from the Comfort fare to Basic Economy with the same times (M-6): a lower class of service is a significant change (260.2); she declined and did not fly, the credit was Tripcairn's, unasked, and Tripcairn charged her card, so it refunds it (260.6, 260.10). Weighted at the fare, 156.00 dollars
